newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - July FTSE options expiry inspires activity.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - July FTSE options expiry inspires activity.

text.p: Forthcoming index options expiry on Friday was responsible for some of the activity in the UK's FTSE 100 index, dealers said.
With mixed expectations as to the direction of the market, other large deals in the index were put and call spreads from separate traders.
One trader sold 5,000 July 4975 calls at around 20p to buy calls in the September series.
Traders with different views on the short-term direction of the market took positions with July call spreads. One deal was to buy 1,500 July 5025/5050 calls at 5p.
The deal will make a maximum 20p profit if the market goes above 5050 by Friday's 0930 GMT expiry.
Another trader initiated the reverse deal by selling 500 July 5025/5050 calls at 5p which will also be the maximum profit if the market stays below 5025.
There was also a seller of a total of 2,500 July 5025 puts at various prices between 45p and 55p who will collect the option premiums if the market goes above 5025.
Away from near-term options activity, in the FTSE there was a large volatility trade involving a total of about 1,000 December 4525/4925 puts bought at prices around 100p.
These put spreads were hedged by buying September FTSE futures at prices between 4985 and 4995.
The deal will make money if market volatility increases.
By 1400 GMT, cash FTSE was down 9.7 to 4954.5 while September futures were down 36 points to 4980.
